purpose: Test whether fitting source-defined semantic parts preserves later part and union judgments better than fitting source atoms or only their sum.
threshold_source_split: 16 geometry candidates/source member;2 retained/source member; ordinary constrained quadratic fit, no biography labels or outputs in fitting
statistics_unit: 695 development biographies; same source, target seed and classifier. All requests remain paired per document.
budget: Natural-state correspondence plus fixed source-head dev evaluation;1200driver seconds, under1GB transient state, gpu-0 lease.
scope: Development only on the unchanged R58 final target dictionary stack, fixed source classifier and 695 exposed biographies. Same 128 natural sequences, clean/full source path, candidate pool and at most 110 target members. Part and total fits start from the same atom-fit relation; total fit retains that initialization rather than inventing a part allocation. Raw retains every source column and accepts the same source-defined parts and unions. No test data, target biography labels or task outputs enter fitting. New unions are evaluated without fitting their trajectories; one target seed, not a confirmation. Native_refit receives the same additional solver iterations and warm-started support refit as the two grouped fits; original native remains separately visible.
